finding_reviews.rationale: Fund-level finding; the ledger row is the only affected unit (0001916099/2024-12-31/pct_of_net_assets_sum), matching the report. I checked 0000950170-25-038029 myself (scratch/fund_runs/0001916099/review/pct_facts.py): 31 InvestmentOwnedPercentOfNetAssets facts for 2024-12-31, all on aggregate contexts (no instrument word in any member), none on a position; the published quarter has 0 of 90 rows with a percent. Printed position lines end at fair value; the percent is printed on industry subtotals and totals. The verdict's cited lines are the two totals. A07 is silent here because the check skips funds with no published percent (D-002); the finding stays outstanding only through the unretired real-error verdict. The check does not misfire, so this is not a check-repair case under the 2026-11-04 ruling. The condition is real and as filed: there is no per-position percent to extract, and the 2024-03-31 10-Q also tags none (11 aggregate facts), so the fund never printed one. Two caveats for the orchestrator. (1) The precedent for this exact pattern is a D-252 retirement of the verdict, not a disposition: Blue Owl VR-FL-1812554-10 (D-266) and 0001869453 (standing_rule_fundloop_0001869453_2026-11-14.json). That route was open to the investigator and is the cleaner close. (2) The proposal's reason key 'coverage-percent-of-net-assets-no-longer-printed' is factually off for this fund: nothing stopped being printed, because it never was. Re-key it, or route it to the owner rather than letting the check accept it automatically.

The other two are harmless (no published row changes), but A01's rollup population drops by one in each of the three quarters (11->10, 12->11, 18->17). The orchestrator should know this is a fund-config change that takes a rollup out of a rule's scope. A01 remains the right detector for the misclassification elsewhere.

request_reviews.rationale: Confirmed from the code. scripts/v05_evidence/make_batch_dispositions.py builds entries with only a query-evidence string and no rows or filing quotes, and without legacy_unscoped. It then asserts fd.validate(entry) is empty (line 88). pipeline/finding_dispositions._validate_bar requires a filing quote per member and a rows list for any non-legacy as_filed/not_applicable entry. So any newly passing quarter makes the tool stop with AssertionError. The existing entry DS-FUNDLOOP-C107-1916099 is legacy_unscoped and frozen to its members, so it cannot simply absorb a new quarter either. This is a defect in the verification tooling, not a request to weaken the D-253 bar, so verification_bug is the right class. The fix must emit per-member quotes and rows (or route the quarter to a proposal), with a test that a source-backed entry validates and a quote-less one still fails. Weakness: the request's evidence quote (Kelso, 0000950170-25-107866) shows an undrawn line but says nothing about the tool; the evidence is code, not the filing. I did not run the tool (it writes to the store).

The header prints only '(Amounts in thousands, except share data)', with no currency. As written this is the inference the D-252 bar does not allow. My independent reading supports the USD conclusion, so the fix is to re-issue the entry with that evidence and a check that reads it: (a) the XBRL principal fact for context C_9a49e5b7-ed05-4bc3 is tagged unit U_USD (bdc_holdings.csv principal_amount_unit, all three Purflux quarters); (b) principal moves 54,619 -> 53,721 -> 52,472 while cost moves 52,265 -> 52,331 -> 51,952, which is the pattern of a translated euro par, not a paydown; (c) fair value/par is 97.6-99.7 pct each quarter; (d) EUR forwards are sold (35,419 and 35,000 thousand EUR). I expect a re-issued entry to pass. Until then, the finding should not count as cleared by this entry.
